title: Drive-Cycle Battery-to-Shaft Efficiency of a Full-Bridge Reconfigurable DC Battery
content: Reconfigurable Battery System (RBS) can act as a variable DC source that keeps the DC-link voltage of an electric drivetrain quasi-constant, which is expected to improve drivetrain efficiency. Whether this yields a higher battery-to-shaft efficiency over complete drive cycles has rarely been quantified. This work compares a full-bridge RBS with a conventional Battery Pack (BP) supplying the same two-level inverter and axial-flux permanent-magnet machine. A quasi-static backward simulation evaluates both systems over drive cycles and three winding variants of the EMRAX 268. The simulated trends are validated on a drivetrain test bench for three of the cycles. In the simulated drive cycles the BP reaches the same or a slightly higher efficiency, with a maximum difference of 0.2 pp, since the higher cell and switch conduction losses of the RBS outweigh the benefit of the regulated DC link. An RBS advantage appears only for the high-voltage winding at low SoC and high speed. The measurements confirm a 0.6 pp to 0.9 pp higher efficiency of the BP, while the RBS delivers 0.6 % to 3.2 % more mechanical energy before cut-off. The benefits of the RBS are thus a stable DC-link voltage and a higher usable energy, not a efficiency gain.
